key_insight: Simple, oriented rectangular occlusions can effectively fool image classifiers without access to their internal workings. STROKE reports high attack success with low query counts at nominal 1–2% image-area settings.
problem_solved: Testing image classifiers with small occlusion-based adversarial attacks can require many model queries when internal parameters and gradients are unavailable.
method: Construct sparse perturbations using simple, oriented rectangular occlusions.
Use model output scores to guide a lightweight greedy procedure that adds and refines occlusions.
Evaluate attack success and query counts across diverse image classifiers, including comparisons with existing patch-based attacks.
impact: STROKE offers practitioners a query-efficient way to probe classifier robustness to small, structured occlusions. The reported results show favorable performance against existing patch-based attacks in several configurations.
visual_elements: Before-and-after image pair highlighting rectangular occlusions and the resulting prediction change.
Workflow diagram: add rectangle → query model scores → refine occlusion → repeat.
Attack-success-versus-query-count chart comparing STROKE with patch-based baselines, using reported results.
Image-area graphic illustrating nominal 1–2% occlusion settings.
paper_title: STROKE: Simple Sparse Structural Occlusions for Black-Box Adversarial Attacks
paper_authors: Ankit Gupta, Akshat Pandya, Paul Lin, Christoph Adami, Emily Dolson
